_comment: Specialization talk (NPCConversation SpecTalk). {spec} is the specialization's name as the player reads it (a weapon spec reads its weaponTopic instead), {level} its tier name (Advanced, Master), {name} the other person in a question and answer. Pools are keyed by voice group: boastful, humble, analytical, warm, wry, playful, plus em and bubba, who keep their own voice.

boastful: Nobody in this town comes close to me at {spec}. {Nobody|Not one of them}.
{level} at {spec}. Say it slowly, it sounds even better.
Ask anyone who is best at {spec}. Actually, don't bother. It's me.
I could do {spec} {in my sleep|with one hand|blindfolded}, and some days I do.
They should put my face on a sign: {spec}, done properly, ask here.
humble: I'm {not bad|alright, I suppose} at {spec}. People keep telling me so, anyway.
{spec} is the one thing I don't mess up. Usually.
Years of {spec} and I still feel like a beginner {some days|most mornings}.
Someone called me an expert in {spec} today. I didn't know where to look.
I just kept practising {spec}. I never meant to get this far with it.
analytical: The trick to {spec} is method. {Ninety|Most} percent of it is doing the boring part properly.
I've been refining how I approach {spec}. {Small margins|Tiny changes}, big difference.
People think {spec} is talent. It's repetition, measured and corrected.
At {level} level, {spec} stops being about rules and starts being about the exceptions.
I keep a mental list of every mistake I've made at {spec}. It is a long list, and a useful one.
warm: I love {spec}. {It's the part of the day that feels like mine|It makes the days feel useful}.
If anyone ever wants to learn {spec}, I'd {happily|gladly} show them.
Years of {spec}, and it still makes me smile when it goes right.
Somebody taught me {spec} once, for nothing. I'm still paying it forward.
Doing {spec} for people I care about is the best part of being good at it.
wry: {level} at {spec}. {Much good it does me|And the rent still comes due}.
Being good at {spec} mostly means everyone asks you to do it for free.
{spec}. I'm good at it. That's the problem, now I'm stuck with it.
All those years of {spec} and the world still hasn't noticed. Fine by me.
Mastering {spec} was easy. Finding anyone who cares, that's the hard part.
playful: {spec} is {basically|just} a game where I know all the cheats.
Give me {spec} and a {free afternoon|quiet corner} and I'll show you something you've never seen.
Every time I do {spec} I try one new thing. {Sometimes it even works|Half the time it goes sideways}.
{spec}? I could talk about it for hours. Don't tempt me.
I dreamt about {spec} last night. Woke up with three new ideas and a headache.
em: {spec}. {level}. I keep notes on my own mistakes, and the notebook is getting thin.
I have {spec} down to a method. I will explain it to anyone who asks, and to some who don't.
{spec} is a system. I have taken it apart twice and put it back better.
If you want {spec} done correctly, I am the correct person. That is a fact, not a boast.
Every time I get better at {spec}, I find a new way to be wrong about it. Fascinating.
bubba: Uè, {spec}? That's my bread an' butter, sugar. {Mannaggia|Madonna}, I'm good at it.
Chiano chiano, that's how you do {spec}. Took me years to learn it the slow way.
{spec}, guaglio'. Like fixin' an engine: listen first, hands second.
Ain't much I'm proud of, but {spec}? That I'll put my name on.
My nonna said I'd never be good at nothin'. Should've seen me at {spec}, sugar.

boastful: Blink and my blade's already back in its sheath. {Nobody|No one here} is faster.
Speed beats size. I've proved it on bigger fools than you.
A knife in my hand {writes its own|signs its own} name. Ask anyone who's met it.
humble: I'm quick with a light blade. It's {not much|nothing special}, I just practise a lot.
Small weapons suit me. I'd rather not need them at all, honestly.
People say I'm fast with a dagger. I just try not to cut myself.
analytical: A light blade trades reach for tempo. You win in the half second they spend deciding.
Footwork first, wrist second. The edge is the least important part of a dagger.
Short weapon, short arcs, no wasted motion. That's all {level} really means.
warm: My first knife was a gift. I keep it sharp, and I keep it for keeping people safe.
I'd teach anyone to handle a small blade. Everybody should be able to look after themselves.
Quick hands are for helping more than hurting. Mostly.
wry: Fast with a knife. Great at parties, terrible for making friends.
Light blades. All the danger, none of the respect.
Years of practice so I can cut bread faster than anyone alive. Worth it.
playful: Watch this, I can flip a dagger {three|four} times and still catch it by the handle. Usually.
A light blade is a dance partner that never steps on your feet.
I once peeled an apple in one strip mid fight. Don't ask how the fight went.

boastful: Show me a swordsman in this town who can touch me. {I'll wait|Go on, I'll wait}.
Guard, cut, thrust. I do all three better than anyone you've ever met.
My sword has never lost a duel. Neither have I, funnily enough.
humble: I know my way around a sword. I'd still rather talk things out.
I've trained with the sword for years. There's always someone better, somewhere.
My teacher would say my guard is still too low. He'd be right.
analytical: Swordplay is geometry with consequences. Angles and distance, nothing more.
Most people watch the blade. Watch the hips, and you'll know the cut before it comes.
The thrust is honest, the cut is forgiving. Knowing which to use is {level} work.
warm: A good sword is a promise to stand between trouble and the people you love.
I still practise with the sword every morning. It clears my head for the day.
Anyone who wants to learn the sword can find me. Bring patience, not pride.
wry: I'm a {level} with a sword. The world moved on to guns and forgot to tell me.
A sword. Heavy on the hip, useless in a queue.
Swordsmanship: the fine art of being very good at something nobody hires for.
playful: Nothing sounds better than a sword leaving its scabbard. {Nothing|Maybe fireworks}.
I name my swords. This one's called Gerald. Gerald has seen things.
I can cut a candle wick without putting the flame out. Party trick, mostly.

boastful: Hand me the biggest thing you've got. I'll swing it all day.
When I commit to a swing, walls {move|give up}. People too.
They built that hammer for two men. I use it for one hand, on bad days.
humble: I'm strong enough for the heavy weapons. That's about all it takes, really.
Big weapons just suit my build. I'm not clever about it.
I try to be gentle with a great hammer. It's harder than it sounds.
analytical: A heavy weapon is momentum management. Stopping the swing is the real skill.
Commit fully or don't swing at all. Half measures with a maul get you killed.
Your spine does the work, not your arms. That took me years to understand.
warm: My big hammer builds fences more often than it breaks anything. I like that.
Carrying the heavy stuff is how I look after my friends. Someone has to.
I'll teach anyone to swing safely. Nobody should wreck their back learning the hard way.
wry: Master of the heavy weapons. My shoulders filed a complaint years ago.
Everyone wants you around when there's something to smash. Never for dinner.
Two handed weapons. Two handed backache.
playful: Nothing like the sound of a great hammer on an anvil. Or a door. Or a wardrobe.
I once split a log, the stump under it, and the ground under that.
Big swing, big grin. That's my whole philosophy.

boastful: Put a hand axe in my fist and I'll clear a forest before lunch.
Nobody chops like me. The trees in this region {know my name|fear my name}.
Weight forward, one swing, done. I don't need a second.
humble: I've a knack with the axe. Grew up splitting wood, that's all it is.
People say I'm good with an axe. I just don't like wasting swings.
The axe and I get along. I don't push it too far, and it doesn't bite me.
analytical: An axe is all head. Let the weight lead and your arms just steer.
The hook behind the blade is the part people forget. Catch the shield, then cut.
Every chop has a best angle. Find it once and you never lose it.
warm: Winter's easier when someone good with an axe lives next door. Happy to be that someone.
My father taught me the axe. I'll teach it to anybody who asks.
There's something honest about an axe. You always know where you stand with it.
wry: {level} with an axe. Everyone treats you like a lumberjack or a murderer.
An axe expert. So I get every splitting job in the street, for the price of a thank you.
The axe never lets me down. People, now, that's another story.
playful: I can land a thrown axe in a target at twenty paces. The trick is not thinking about it.
An axe is just a very serious hat hook. Try it.
I talk to my axe. It hasn't answered yet, but it's a good listener.

boastful: I can crack a whip and snuff a candle across the room. {Every time|First try}.
Reach, crack, wrap. Nobody gets within ten feet of me.
They hear my whip and they reconsider their day.
humble: The whip's an odd skill, I know. I just happen to be alright at it.
I learned the whip on a farm. It's more about patience than anything.
I'm careful with the whip. It's easy to hurt yourself learning it.
analytical: The crack is the tip breaking the sound barrier. Everything else is timing.
A whip is a wave you throw. Control the wave, control the fight.
Entangling is harder than striking. That's where {level} starts to show.
warm: I mostly use the whip to herd goats, honestly. They respect it more than people do.
I'll show you the whip, but slowly. My first lesson left a mark on my ear.
It looks cruel, but in the right hands a whip keeps a crowd safe.
wry: Master of the whip. People assume the worst about me, and they're usually wrong.
The whip. Nobody takes you seriously until you crack it indoors.
Years of practice and I'm still explaining it's not a hobby, it's a discipline.
playful: I can snatch a hat off a head with my whip. I've a small collection now.
Crack! Sorry. Habit. Did that scare you? It was meant to.
A whip's just a very long, very loud finger. I point with it.

boastful: Two ends, and I hit you with both before you blink.
Nobody gets past my staff. Not with a sword, not with a spear, not with a mood.
I've disarmed swordsmen with a broom handle. Imagine what I do with a real staff.
humble: A staff is just a stick. I've only spent a long time with mine.
I'm handy with a staff. It helps on long walks, too.
I don't like to hurt people. A staff lets me stop a fight without much of that.
analytical: The staff is all leverage. Hands wide for power, close for speed.
Every strike on the staff sets up the other end. Think in pairs.
Distance control is everything. Stay at the tip and they can't reach you.
warm: My staff was cut from a tree my grandmother planted. It's family, in a way.
Anyone can learn the staff. Even children. Especially children, they're fearless.
A walking stick by day, a guard by night. I like that it does both.
wry: {level} with a staff. It's a stick. I'm a master of the stick.
Everyone thinks I'm a wizard. I just know how to hit people with wood.
The staff: cheapest weapon, longest apprenticeship.
playful: Spin, spin, sweep. My staff and I make the neighbours dizzy.
I once pole vaulted over a fence with my staff. Missed the other side a bit.
My staff doubles as a washing line. Tactical laundry.

boastful: I can split an arrow already in the target. I've done it {twice|three times} this month.
Draw, anchor, release. Nobody in this region shoots like me.
Name a target, any target. It's already got my arrow in it.
humble: I'm a decent shot with a bow. Good eyes, steady hands, that's all.
The bow's been a quiet friend to me. I don't need to be loud about it.
I still miss sometimes. Don't let anybody tell you they don't.
analytical: Archery is consistency. Same draw, same anchor, same breath, every single time.
Wind, drop and distance. Read those three and the arrow does the rest.
Most misses happen at the release. The fingers have to get out of the way.
warm: Archery calms me down. Just me, the string and the quiet between shots.
My mother taught me to shoot. I love passing it on.
I hunt with the bow so my family eats well. That's what the skill is for.
wry: Master archer. Very useful, right up until it rains.
A bow in the age of guns. I like my lost causes elegant.
People only need an archer when something's already gone wrong.
playful: I can shoot an apple off a hat. I prefer the hat to be on a post.
The best sound in the world is an arrow hitting the centre. Thunk!
I name my arrows too. Losing them is always a small funeral.

boastful: Knives, stars, stones, whatever. If I throw it, it lands where I want.
I hit a coin at thirty paces with a throwing knife. {Tuesday|Last week}, actually.
Nobody throws like me. Nobody even comes close.
humble: I'm alright at throwing things. Not the most useful skill, I know.
Good aim, that's all. I practised on tin cans as a kid.
I throw straight. Everything else about me is a bit crooked.
analytical: A thrown weapon spins at a set rate. Learn your distance in rotations.
Release point beats power every time. Too early, too high. Too late, the floor.
Range weapons are maths you do with your wrist.
warm: I learned to throw with my brother, skipping stones. Still the best days I remember.
Throwing takes patience. I'm happy to be patient with anyone learning.
My aim has kept us fed a few lean winters. Rabbits never see it coming.
wry: Throwing weapons. The only skill where you have to go and fetch it afterwards.
{level} at throwing things. The pub darts board fears me, nothing else does.
Every knife I've ever thrown I've had to walk after. Great exercise.
playful: Pick a knot in that fence. Go on. Any knot.
I juggle throwing knives on slow days. The neighbours have opinions.
Throwing things is just catching, in reverse, for other people.

boastful: I shoot tighter groups than the police range instructors. {They know it|They hate it}.
Pick a bottle on that wall. Pick any bottle. It's gone.
Under pressure I get steadier. That's why I'm the best shot around.
humble: I'm a good shot. I wish it wasn't something I needed to be.
Steady hands and a lot of practice. There's nothing magic about it.
I keep my gun clean and hope I never need it. That's all.
analytical: Trigger control is everything. Squeeze, don't pull. The shot should surprise you.
Breathe out, pause, press. The pause is where the accuracy lives.
Most bad shooting is bad maintenance. Clean the weapon, and half your problems go away.
warm: I teach gun safety to anyone who asks. Knowing is safer than not knowing.
I carry so the people around me don't have to. That's how I see it.
My old shooting coach was the kindest man I ever met. I try to be like him.
wry: Crack shot. The insurance forms all ask about it now.
{level} with a firearm. Makes every argument feel very short.
Being a good shot means you get to clean up after everyone else's bad shots.
playful: I once shot the cork out of a bottle from across a plaza. The wine was terrible.
Tin cans on a fence at sunset. Best way to spend an evening.
I can reload faster than I can tie my shoes. Priorities.

boastful: Close range is my home. Get in there with me and you'll leave in ribbons.
Nobody tears through a guard like I do. {Nobody|Not a soul}.
My claws have opened doors, armour and at least one argument.
humble: I'm good with hand claws. It's not a pretty style, I know.
Claws just fit my hands. I don't go around bragging about it.
I fight close because I'm not good at anything longer. That's the truth of it.
analytical: Claws are about angles. You don't strike through, you rake across.
The fight with claws is won inside their reach. Everything is about the entry.
Grip and wrist strength matter more than the blades on the gauntlet.
warm: They look frightening, but I've only used my claws to protect people. I promise.
Anyone who wants to learn close fighting, I'll show them how to stay safe doing it.
Claws are how I climb, cook and open letters. Fighting is the least of it.
wry: Master of the claws. People cross the street. Can't blame them.
Hand claws. You'll never guess how many gloves I've ruined.
{level} at tearing things. Still can't open a jar.
playful: Rawr. Sorry. Every time I put the claws on I feel like a cat.
I carved my initials into a tree with these. It was a very big tree.
Claws are just knives that high five.

boastful: Nobody lasts three rounds with me. {Nobody|Not one}.
My fists have ended more fights than most people's weapons.
Put the gloves on, square up. Oh, you're busy? Thought so.
humble: I can box a bit. Kept me out of trouble as a kid, mostly.
I'm handy with my fists. I try not to go looking for reasons to use them.
Just a lot of hours at the gym, that's all it is.
analytical: Boxing is feet and breathing. The punches are the least of it.
Jab to measure, cross to finish. Everything else is footnotes.
Tuck the chin, keep the elbows in. It's simple. Doing it tired is the hard part.
warm: I teach the kids at the gym on Saturdays. They're better than me already.
Boxing gave me discipline when I had none. I owe it a lot.
Learning to fight made me calmer, not angrier. Funny how that works.
wry: Good with my fists. Not much good for anything else, according to my mother.
{level} at punching. Surprisingly few job openings.
Every champion's nose looks like mine eventually.
playful: Float, sting, the usual. I've a better rhyme but it's rude.
I shadow box in shop windows. People think I'm waving at them.
My gloves have names. Left is Thunder, right is also Thunder. Easier that way.

boastful: Nobody gets inside my reach. {Nobody alive|Nobody yet}.
Reach, thrust, set. I could hold a bridge on my own with a spear.
Bring a sword against my spear. I'd love to see how that goes for you.
humble: The spear's a simple weapon. I'm just stubborn about practising it.
I'm decent with a spear. It's the oldest weapon there is, anybody can learn it.
Long reach suits a cautious person. I'm very cautious.
analytical: A spear is distance you can hold. Keep the point on the line and they have to go around it.
Setting the butt against a charge is physics doing your work for you.
Short grip for speed, long grip for reach. {level} means switching without thinking.
warm: Fishing with a spear on a quiet morning is my favourite thing in the world.
My grandfather's spear hangs over my door. I keep it oiled for him.
A spear wall only works if everyone trusts each other. I like that about it.
wry: Master of the spear. Try getting it on a bus.
The spear: great in a phalanx, terrible in a corridor.
Oldest weapon in the world, and I'm the last one in town who takes it seriously.
playful: I can knock an apple off a branch with the butt of my spear and catch it on the point.
Spear fishing, spear hunting, spear reaching things off high shelves.
Every spear is secretly a very long fork.

boastful: {name}, I'm nearly as good as you at {spec}. Nearly. What's the one thing I'm missing?
Alright, {name}, {spec}. Show me the trick and I'll be better than you by spring.
They say you're the best at {spec}, {name}. Prove it: what's the secret?
{name}. {spec}. Give me one tip, just one, and I'll take it from there.
humble: Um, {name}? Sorry to bother you. How did you get so good at {spec}?
{name}, could I ask you something about {spec}? I keep getting it wrong.
I'm still hopeless at {spec}, {name}. Where would you even start?
If it's not too much trouble, {name}, what should a beginner practise in {spec}?
analytical: {name}, in {spec}, what do beginners get wrong that they don't notice?
Genuine question, {name}: in {spec}, what matters more, speed or precision?
{name}, how do you know when you've actually improved at {spec}?
What's the part of {spec} that the books never explain, {name}?
warm: {name}, I've been trying {spec} lately. Any advice for someone just starting out?
You're so good at {spec}, {name}. Would you ever show me a little?
{name}, what made you fall in love with {spec}?
I'd love to get better at {spec}, {name}. What helped you most?
wry: {name}, go on. Tell me {spec} isn't as hard as it looks. Lie if you have to.
So, {name}, {spec}. Is it worth the bother, or am I wasting my time?
{name}, how many years of {spec} before it stops being miserable?
Tell me honestly, {name}. Is anyone actually good at {spec}, or do you all just pretend?
playful: {name}! Teach me one {spec} trick. A flashy one. Please?
Quick, {name}: what's the coolest thing you can do with {spec}?
{name}, if {spec} was a game, what's the cheat code?
I tried {spec} yesterday and it went sideways, {name}. What did I do wrong?
em: {name}. {spec}. I have three questions and I would like them answered in order.
Explain {spec} to me, {name}. Do not simplify it. I will know.
{name}, I have been studying {spec}. Where does my method fail?
Your {spec} is better than mine, {name}. I would like to know exactly why.
bubba: Uè, {name}, you're good at {spec}, eh? How's a fella learn that?
{name}, sugar, {spec}. What's the trick? I'm a mechanic, I like to see the insides.
Mannaggia, {name}, I tried {spec} an' made a mess of it. Where'd I go wrong?
Chiano chiano, {name}. Walk me through {spec}, like you'd explain a carburettor.

boastful: Easy, {name}. Watch me do {spec} and copy everything. Everything.
The secret to {spec}? Be me. Failing that, practise every day for ten years.
You're asking the right person, {name}. Lesson one: never doubt yourself.
Hah! Stick close, {name}. A bit of my {spec} might rub off on you.
humble: Oh, I'm really not that good, {name}. Just practise the basics until they're boring.
Honestly, {name}? I made every mistake first. Just keep at it.
I don't know if I'm the one to ask, {name}, but slow down. That helped me.
Start small, {name}. That's all I did, really.
analytical: Break it down, {name}. Master one piece of {spec} at a time and measure each one.
Precision first, {name}. Speed comes from repetition, never the other way round.
Keep notes, {name}. Every mistake you write down is one you won't make twice.
Most people rush the fundamentals of {spec}, {name}. Don't.
warm: Of course, {name}! Come by any time and we'll practise together.
Be kind to yourself, {name}. Everyone is terrible at {spec} at first.
I'd love to help, {name}. Bring a friend, it's more fun that way.
What helped me most was someone patient. I'll be that for you, {name}.
wry: The secret, {name}? Years of boredom and a bit of bad luck.
Keep failing, {name}. Eventually you run out of ways to get it wrong.
Honestly, {name}, it's worth it. Just don't expect anyone to thank you.
Nobody's good at first, {name}. Most of us aren't even good at the end.
playful: Watch closely, {name}. No, closer. Now forget everything and try it your own way.
The cheat code, {name}? Practise until it feels like playing.
Try it backwards, {name}. Seriously. You'll learn more from the mess.
Ha! Come find me tomorrow, {name}. I'll show you the flashy bit.
em: Your method fails at the second step, {name}. Everyone's does. Fix that first.
{spec} is a system, {name}. Learn the system and the rest is arithmetic.
Write down what you do, {name}, then do exactly that. Most people cannot.
Three rules, {name}: observe, repeat, correct. In that order. Always.
bubba: Chiano chiano, {name}. Listen first, hands second. Same as an engine.
Uè, sugar, you don't learn {spec} from talkin'. Grab it an' get your hands dirty.
Mannaggia, {name}, everybody wants the trick. There ain't one. Just time.
Come by the camper, guaglio'. I'll show you proper, with coffee.
